statement: A project key is one or more characters, uppercase ASCII letters and digits only, starting with a letter. It is the immutable prefix of every ticket key and of every ticket directory name, so the project validator and the ticket-path validator enforce the same rule.
lengthIsNotPartOfTheGrammar: An existing project keeps whatever key length it was created with, so neither validator caps length. The creation surfaces cap a new key at creationMaxLength for readability, and key derivation produces at most derivationMaxLength characters.
readers: apps/desktop/src/tickets.ts via apps/desktop/src/tickets.test.ts (the valid ticketKeys and the ticketKeySuffix block; the invalid rows are the directory grammar's, and the palette deliberately accepts more — it takes lc-42 and LC-211P, which a folder name may not be)

keys.note: digits are legal after the first character
longer than the creation cap; the grammar still accepts it, so an existing project stays openable

ticketKeys.note: a digit inside the prefix is legal
the prefix must satisfy the project-key grammar, so the two validators cannot disagree
no leading zero in the number
the minted shape: a number and one lowercase trailing character (LC-232)
a suffix sits behind a prefix that carries a digit
o is dropped from the minting alphabet as a confusable and is still readable: the reader accepts more than the allocator draws
macOS folds case, so an uppercase suffix would be a second key on one directory
the no-leading-zero rule survives the suffix
a suffix is not a number
one character is the length that was chosen
a suffix does not make a second segment legal

ticketKeySuffix.statement: A ticket key is <KEY>-<n> or <KEY>-<n><s>, where n carries no leading zero and s is a single lowercase ASCII letter. Keys minted from 2026-08-25 carry s; LC-1 through LC-233 predate it and keep the keys they were minted with, so the reader accepts both forms.
ticketKeySuffix.caseNote: Lowercase only. fs::create_dir is how a key is claimed and macOS folds case, so LC-211p and LC-211P would be two keys on one directory.
ticketKeySuffix.droppedNote: l and o sit next to the 1 and the 0 already in a key that people read aloud, type into `ticket show`, and paste into commit messages.
ticketKeySuffix.collisionOdds: Two branches that both take max+1 agree on the number and then differ on the letter 23 times out of 24 — about 4% of those collisions survive. `longclaw ticket renumber` carries the remainder.
